newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania hits out at Italy over refugee boat sinking.
newsitem.headline: Albania hits out at Italy over refugee boat sinking.

text.p: Albania, angry over the sinking of a refugee boat in the Adriatic, told Italy on Saturday that the accident could have been avoided and that the guilty should be identified.
Prime Minister Bashkim Fino went on television to tell his enraged country that he wanted an Italian inquiry into the incident in which at least four Albanians died. Thirty-four people were rescued.
Survivors said dozens of others had been on the boat, which sank after colliding with an Italian navy corvette that was trying to intercept it on Friday night.

"I appreciate Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi's statement and I ask his cabinet to start investigations so that the guilty be identified. I still insist the tragedy should have been avoided," Fino said.
Albanian Deputy Foreign Minister Pavllo Zeri summoned the Italian ambassador, Paolo Foresti, and told him the Italian government must take steps to prevent such tragedies in future.
Parliamentary speaker Pjeter Arbnori strongly criticised Italy, saying: "The boat should have been accompanied to Italy's coast instead of being blocked."

The semi-official Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano said the deaths of the Albanian refugees were an "avoidable tragedy", and criticised the "bureaucratic slowness and indifference of part of the international community."
"It is necessary and urgent to help the Albanian people because every lost day brings catastrophe closer," it said.
The Italian navy has been turning back Albanian refugees fleeing by boat across the Adriatic to escape unrest which has swept their country over the past month.
The incident occurred just as Italy was beginning to put together a multinational force to protect humanitarian aid operations in Albania.
Many of those on the ill-fated boat came from the port of Vlore, one of the spots where the multinational force is to be deployed.

Italy was given a green light by the United Nations on Friday to go ahead and organise the multinational force, which Rome feels is essential to stabilising Albania and preventing a flood of illegal immigrants.
More than 13,000 illegal Albanians have risked the trip across the Adriatic in boats since March 13, when a popular uprising swept the south of Albania and then spread north.
Prodi said on Saturday that the sinking of the refugee boat had made an international mission to help Albania more urgent.
He also told reporters that the navy operation to patrol the southern Adriatic and stem a tide of refugees would continue because it had Albanian government approval.
"This event shows that the international operation to help Albania has to begin as soon as possible," Prodi said.
